ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $PA$ is the tangent line to $\odot O$ at point $A$, and $PO$ intersects $\odot O$ at point $B$. Given $\tan P = \frac{3}{4}$ and $OB = 6$, what is the length of $PB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $PA$ is the tangent of circle $O$ with A as the point of tangency,\\
thus $OA\perp AP$,\\
hence $\angle OAP=90^\circ$\\
In $\triangle OAP$,\\
since $\tan P=\frac{OA}{AP}=\frac{3}{4}$ and $OA=OB=6$,\\
we have $\frac{6}{AP}=\frac{3}{4}$,\\
therefore $AP=8$,\\
thus $OP=\sqrt{OA^{2}+AP^{2}}=10$,\\
hence $PB=OP-OB=10-6=\boxed{4}$.

hence $\angle OAP=90^\circ$\\

since $\tan P=\frac{OA}{AP}=\frac{3}{4}$ and $OA=OB=6$,\\

thus $OP=\sqrt{OA^{2}+AP^{2}}=10$,\\

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a circle with center O, A is located below the circle, and the horizontal line segment AP through A is tangent to the circle, with P on the right side outside the circle. Segment OP is an oblique line, passing through point B on the circle, and B is between O and P. It can also be seen that OA is the radius from the center of the circle to the point of tangency A. Reasoning: Because PA is the tangent to circle O at point A, the radius OA is perpendicular to the tangent AP, that is, triangle OAP is right-angled at A. Also because OA and OB are both radii of the circle, and OB = 6, so OA = 6. In right triangle OAP, the tangent of angle P is tan P = opposite side/adjacent side = OA/AP = 6/AP. It is known that tan P = 3/4, so 6/AP = 3/4, solving gives AP = 8. Thus OP = sqrt(OA^2 + AP^2) = sqrt(6^2 + 8^2) = 10. Since in the figure B is on OP and is between O and P, PB = OP - OB = 10 - 6 = 4.
